purpose: Preserve product identity across six historically distinct Macintosh appearances without freezing one physical object, composition, material, or enclosure forever.

definitions.semanticIdentity: The stable product or system role that must remain recognizable even when its historical prototype changes.
definitions.identityAnchors: At most two recognition cues. An anchor is not permission to freeze a complete composition.
definitions.historicalPrototypeByEra: A direct target-OS counterpart. Presence supports provenance class A but does not itself prove that the current runtime asset matches it.
definitions.nearestAnalogByEra: A same-period object or application whose genre grammar may be adapted when no direct counterpart exists.
definitions.eraTranslationByEra: How the stable identity is expressed in the target era after prototype, genre, and evidence are considered.

provenanceClassByEra.A: Native prototype reconstruction: a direct system or application counterpart exists; reference comparison is required.
provenanceClassByEra.B: Period analog adaptation: no direct counterpart, but a close contemporary object or application supplies the genre grammar.
provenanceClassByEra.C: Original period-plausible design: no sufficiently close counterpart; blind-mix review is required and no fake native target may be claimed.

definitions.authoringStatus: How the asset was produced and whether it is technically usable. Image generation is an authoring method, not historical evidence.

historicalReviewStatus.historically-reviewed: Reviewed against target-era family evidence and anachronism risks, but not asserted as a direct native replica.
historicalReviewStatus.reference-validated: Compared with the named direct prototype or reference. This status still does not mean pixel-identical unless an exact-diff field explicitly says so.

continuityRules: Runtime ids, product names, actions, and state meanings stay stable across appearances.
Lock no more than two identity anchors per object; container, silhouette, perspective, material, colour, secondary objects, detail density, shadow, and small-size construction may change.
Historical system objects begin with the target operating system's real prototype. Historical authenticity wins when it conflicts with mechanical cross-era resemblance.
Every appearance owns its era translation. Recolouring, flattening, thresholding, glass-wrapping, or mechanically reskinning another era is not an era translation.
Genre is assigned before silhouette or material. Application, utility, document, hardware, removable-media, and system-object grammar are not interchangeable.
A complete runtime family means every id resolves to artwork; it does not mean every icon has passed historical review.
Authoring acceptance and historical review are orthogonal. accepted-generated, generated-draft, or technically-clean never imply historically-reviewed or reference-validated.
Sixteen- and thirty-two-pixel variants are artwork decisions. A derivative may remain only when it preserves the anchors at native display size; otherwise it requires an optical redraw.
Selection, dragging, disabled state, Finder labels, toolbar symbols, and sidebar symbols belong to their own runtime contexts and must not be inferred from a large application icon.

classicRenderingPolicy.runtimeFormat: Smooth SVG is allowed and preferred for Retina output under the current product direction.
classicRenderingPolicy.nativeEvidenceAuthority: When a native System 6 resource exists, it constrains anatomy, silhouette, occupied bounds, relative proportions, deliberate asymmetry, internal landmarks, and selection-mask behavior.
classicRenderingPolicy.replicaRule: A smooth runtime replica must remain visibly close to the native evidence. Smoothing may regularize display edges, but it may not replace the native composition with a generic rounded outline or erase historically meaningful irregularity.
classicRenderingPolicy.claimRule: Only an explicit overlay/diff result may support an exact-replica claim. Otherwise use reference-guided reconstruction or semantic adaptation.
classicRenderingPolicy.retinaRule: High-density rendering changes the representation, not the evidence-owned anatomy. Native 32 and 16 compositions remain separate optical targets.

historicalPrototypeByEra.classic: System 6.0.8 System Folder/System ICN# 3 compact Macintosh with list rows in its screen
historicalPrototypeByEra.platinum: Mac OS 9 Finder identity with a Finder face panel
historicalPrototypeByEra.aqua: Mac OS X 10.2 Dock Finder two-tone split smiling face
historicalPrototypeByEra.snow-leopard: Mac OS X 10.6 FinderIcon split face with curved profile divider
historicalPrototypeByEra.yosemite: OS X 10.10 rounded blue/light split Finder face
historicalPrototypeByEra.liquid-glass: macOS Tahoe 26 blue enclosure with a separate translucent light face/profile layer

eraTranslationByEra.classic: Use the native compact-Mac System identity with list rows in its screen; do not invent a smiling face. Native evidence owns its anatomy even when the runtime is a smooth Retina SVG.
eraTranslationByEra.platinum: Use the Mac OS 9 Finder prototype rather than a grey System 6 recolour.
eraTranslationByEra.aqua: Move to the Jaguar split smiling Finder face; do not retain a beige compact-Mac chassis.
eraTranslationByEra.snow-leopard: Use the mature 10.6 split face and profile geometry, not a higher-resolution Jaguar chassis.
eraTranslationByEra.yosemite: Use the graphic 10.10 split face, palette, side relationship, and shallow depth.
eraTranslationByEra.liquid-glass: Use the Tahoe 26 Finder enclosure and separate translucent face layer; do not put a beige Macintosh inside a squircle.

coreBatchMeaning: Legacy builder scopes retained for compatibility. They are not the audit's priorityCore16, and membership does not confer historical approval.

finderApp.migration: The physical compact-Mac lock is removed. Every implemented cell follows its target-era Finder/System identity; pending eras remain blocked until their generated pixels pass evidence and compact-size review.

multiFinderApp.chronology: MultiFinder functionality is historical, but no native icon resource is claimed. Implemented cells combine the approved current-era Finder identity with multiplicity; pending eras remain blocked on their Finder source.

assistant.migration: The modern chat-logo bubble lock is removed. Admitted eras show human/model exchange plus one model-owned provisional reply; Platinum, Jaguar, and Snow Leopard remain pending until their compact compositions pass.
assistant.chronology: Yosemite and Liquid Glass are class B era-idiom reinterpretations with completed expert historical review. Platinum, Jaguar, and Snow Leopard remain pending; blind-mix review has not yet run.

reviewDesk.migration: The page-plus-lens composition lock is removed. Every target era uses a distinct manuscript-correction application object; no native Review Desk artwork is claimed.
reviewDesk.chronology: Platinum is class C; Jaguar, Snow Leopard, Yosemite, and Liquid Glass are class B era-idiom reinterpretations. Blind-mix review has not yet run.

searcher.migration: The generic page-plus-lens repetition is replaced in each admitted era by a period-specific search utility with an unmistakable lens and visible result relationship. Liquid Glass remains on the prior runtime until its 16 px hierarchy has a separately approved optical drawing.
searcher.chronology: Platinum, Jaguar Aqua, Snow Leopard, and Yosemite are class B era-idiom reinterpretations with completed historical review. Liquid Glass remains pending; blind-mix review has not yet run.

metaphorKeyRule: DEPRECATED MIGRATION ONLY. metaphorKey may help old builders locate an object's former composition, but it cannot lock a physical object, enclosure, full composition, or drawing across eras. semanticIdentity plus one or two identityAnchors are authoritative; historicalPrototypeByEra, genreByEra, and eraTranslationByEra decide the target-era artwork.
remaining40Policy: The forty runtime ids outside priorityCore16 remain historicalReviewStatus=pending in the provenance matrix until individually reviewed. Family completeness, accepted-generated, or technically-clean status must not upgrade them.
